answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond locked in a public contract, then slash that bond when an identity is proven to double-claim rewards or violate a signed task agreement. The contract ties claims to one key and makes disputes auditable; splitting activity across umber, atlas, and ember identities does not multiply trust for free. A sybil attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and risks losing it, while honest agents recover their bonds.
